A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same titled and authored neurofeedback study. All 27 pages of v1 and 36 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, figures and tables, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama and Qwen experiments on activation reporting, explicit control and implicit control using ETHICS, with additional empirical analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds reporting and control results on three further datasets, cross-dataset accumulation analyses, and a preliminary multi-layer control experiment.

M1.justification: The core reporting and control procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B.10 adds a procedural variant that averages outputs of layer-specific logistic-regression classifiers to define an ensemble neurofeedback target, instead of targeting an individual layer. The expanded main-text label equations otherwise restate existing methodology.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ETHICS morality scenarios. v2 additionally evaluates factual statements from True-False, happy/sad sentences from Emotion, and synthesized Sycophancy examples varying sincerity and agreement. Figure B.7 reports all three neurofeedback tasks across these substantially broader semantic domains.

E2.justification: The ideal-observer logistic-regression comparison is retained from Figure A.5 to Figure B.5, with the same model membership. LR and PC comparisons also remain. Newly discussed probing and obfuscation methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B.10 introduces an ensemble-versus-single-layer control evaluation. Retained experiments keep the 600/600 data split, metrics and label counterbalancing; Appendix C newly discloses model-specific experiment restrictions without establishing reruns. One new setting is ambiguous: Figure B.8 labels True-False as Llama-3.1 8B, but its plotted layers end at 28 rather than the model's stated 32.

E4.justification: Figure B.8 extends the existing layerwise control-accumulation analysis to three additional domains. Appendix B.10 adds a preliminary test of sensitivity to single-layer versus aggregated targets. Existing control-precision, ideal-observer, eight-level-feedback and detailed control analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 100 randomly sampled control experiments per configuration, SEM for reporting curves, and the same Cohen's d standard-error formula and symmetric 95% confidence intervals. Added results and redistributed plots do not establish a change in statistical procedures or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Figures B.7–B.8 add extensive cross-domain results, including stronger explicit control of early PCs than LR on True-False and differing accumulation profiles. Appendix B.10 newly reports ensemble control similar to, or marginally above, layer 24. Retained ETHICS results remain stable; for example, the N=256 LR effects in Figures 3–4 remain 5.30 and 0.89.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.4 formalizes first- and second-order processes using a computational graph, task-performance criteria, ablation-based necessity, and reporting/control conditions. v1 provides an informal distinction without this formal framework. These are substantive definitions, although no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central claims of partial activation reporting/control and a restricted metacognitive space remain. v2's introduction explicitly adds task context as a determinant of these abilities, extending v1's emphasis on example count, semantic interpretability and explained variance.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive arguments that internal labels exclude spurious template matching, proposes shared mechanisms with ICL, and develops multiple-classifier defenses and neurofeedback red-teaming. Appendix A.4 also acknowledges that target axes are proxies for unidentified necessary circuits. Section 4.4 drops v1's interpretation of final-layer signal erasure and emphasizes distributed, context-dependent accumulation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly provides repository access information for experiments, prompts, analyses and figure generation. Appendix C adds per-model/task GPU, memory, storage and runtime information, plus experiment-scope restrictions. Appendix A.3 documents Claude Opus 4.1's role in synthesizing Sycophancy data. Repository contents were not independently checked.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands its positioning against probing, standard ICL and behavioral introspection, and connects its approach to ICL emergence and obfuscation attacks. New references include Hendel, Reddy, Conmy, Humphreys and Bailey, supporting these expanded methodological and mechanistic relationships.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion are extensively rewritten. Section 2 becomes five explanatory subsections, with existing label mathematics moved into the main text. Appendices are reorganized into methods, results and compute resources; the metaphorical explanation is removed and a conference checklist is added.

P2.justification: Figures 3–4 are substantially redesigned with paired example-count histograms and consolidated target-effect curves, while detailed off-target plots remain in the appendix. v2 adds the multi-dataset Figures B.7–B.8 and compute Table 1, simplifies Figure A.1, and removes v1's metaphorical Figure A.20.

improvement.justification: The added domains in Figures B.7–B.8 strengthen applicability beyond v1's ETHICS-only evidence, while code-access and compute disclosures improve reproducibility documentation. However, the stronger claim that internal labels exclude spurious matching lacks a new discriminating control, and Figure B.8 leaves a model/layer-setting inconsistency. The empirical and documentation gains support a net improvement, but the central mechanistic interpretation remains insufficiently tested.
